still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent Medicare obesity benefit. Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes, and the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: ever 30.6 − current 19.0 = 11.6% of adults used and are off now. ~55% of current users are on a second or later course (10.5 pts), ~2.8 pts cycled and are off again, so (10.5 + 2.8) / 30.6 ≈ 43.5% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~8.8 pts stopped once and have not restarted. That fits one-year persistence near one-third on weekly and oral products and 36–47% restarting within a year. The cycled share dips from 45% because ~1.8 pts of new first-time users came in, mostly through Medicaid waivers and calm/AUD plans. Age check: 0.20×10.5 + 0.33×18.5 + 0.24×28 + 0.23×17.5 = 2.1 + 6.1 + 6.7 + 4.0 ≈ 19.0. Income thirds average 19.0 and bracket the national figure. 19.0% of ~274M adults ≈ 52.1M users, down ~1.2M from 53.3M. Channel changes behind the net figure: gray market −2.3M (7.5M → 5.2M), commercial −1.4M (13.9M → 12.5M), Medicare +0.3M (11.2M → 11.5M), Medicaid +1.0M (3.2M → 4.2M, ~0.8M of it in the new 1115 waivers), legitimate cash +1.2M (17.6M → 18.8M, including ~2.1M on calm/AUD plans). Payer mix: commercial ~24%, Medicare ~22%, Medicaid ~8%, cash ~36%, gray ~10%. Off-drug population: ~1.4M long-term semaglutide users are on planned 12-month 'elastase holidays' and are counted as off. ~0.3M waiver enrollees were dropped for missing the 5% milestone, and about half of them went back to vials. ~22% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the rural South outside the waiver states and among adults 65+ without CVD codes. Adult obesity is ~33.0%. Pediatric: ~1.0% of under-18s are on a drug, ~2.3% of 12–17s and ~0.15% of 6–11s. About 4.8M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, and ~1.1M live with a parent currently on a pancreatic holiday.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~11.5M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 11.5M × ~$225 average net/month × 12 ≈ $31.1B a year gross Part D incretin spend, roughly flat on 2032 because net prices fell ~4%/yr while users grew. The dementia route is ~2.0M × ~$235 × 12 ≈ $5.6B. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight-loss use under the state plan. Five more (Tennessee, Louisiana, West Virginia, Oklahoma, Arkansas) run CMS-approved 'Metabolic Health' 1115 waivers that give Foundayo free to adults ≤200% FPL with BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with prediabetes, conditional on weekly app check-ins and ≥5% loss at the 6-month weigh-in. Waiver arithmetic: ~0.8M enrollees × ~$139 net (supplemental rebate) × 12 ≈ $1.33B a year, ~68% federal ≈ $0.9B. Budget neutrality rests on projected diabetes-onset savings that CBO has not scored. Total Medicaid users ~4.2M.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across ~130 brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials run $15–50, and Chinese retatrutide-analogue 'research peptide' vials appeared in 2033 at $40–80. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China supply roughly 70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued through the April 2034 TrumpRx repricing: Wegovy pill maintenance $199 → $179, Foundayo $139–199, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $229–279, retatrutide (all doses including the new 12 mg) $399 → $299 cash direct, MariTide direct $249 → $229. Oral Wegovy starts stay $149. Novo's AUD brand Steadra (low-dose oral semaglutide) is $149 on TrumpRx. Amycretin is on commercial formularies with prior authorisation. Employer weight coverage fell from 30% to 27% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2033). About 70% of the employers that still cover now require verified adherence plus a BMI milestone, and a further ~13% of employers cover only through monitored metabolic tracks. Tracks hold ~6.4M enrollees inside the 12.5M commercial users, ~4.4M of them on clinic-administered MariTide (5.2M MariTide users in total). Cash and calm: ~2.1M on calm/focus or Steadra-anchored plans ($149–179 fill + $39–59 platform fee). Gray market ~5.2M. It fell because waiver states absorbed ~0.6M former vial users and seizures rose, and because 2031's bad batches still deter buyers. Retatrutide analogues and cloned pens keep it significant.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg high-dose maintenance approved Jan 2034)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; Steadra low-dose oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, approved Mar 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, lean-mass adjunct to incretin therapy (bimagrumab, approved Oct 2033)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; growth-monitoring labelling)

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide); the confirmatory trial read out Sep 2034 (HR ~0.88), with resubmission for 60+ without CVD planned for 2035
alcohol use disorder: reduction in heavy drinking days (low-dose oral semaglutide, Steadra, Mar 2033), the first approved reward-modulation indication
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'quiet mind' plans, now often written as Steadra on a screening-questionnaire AUD diagnosis or as off-label Foundayo, ~2.1M subscribers
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash and gray
planned 'elastase holidays': deliberate 12-month breaks after 5+ years of semaglutide, which are a clinical practice rather than a drug use
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity, still falling
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen launch: no new molecule could launch in this window, so the ~30% triple-agonist driver is realised by an existing product in a new form. Lilly filed a retatrutide 12 mg high-dose maintenance sNDA in Nov 2032 and it was approved in Jan 2034, 14 months later, with ~28.7% mean weight loss on the label (TRIUMPH programme) and new dysaesthesia and heart-rate language. Mood/motivation: oral semaglutide for AUD, filed Jan 2032, was approved Mar 2033 as the separate brand Steadra. It is the first label that names reduced craving as the benefit, and the calm industry built on it. Lilly filed Foundayo for moderate-to-severe binge-eating disorder in Mar 2034, with a decision no earlier than Mar 2035. Bimagrumab, filed Jul 2032, was approved Oct 2033 as a lean-mass adjunct. It preserves ~3–4 percentage points more lean mass, lists at ~$1,150, and is mostly covered only inside premium tracks. Implants remain phase 1–2 and are not on the market, and no new generic exists in the US. The global incretin market is ~$182B (2033). US net prices keep drifting down 3–5% a year and brands hold above ~$139.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Rates on retatrutide 12 mg run higher during titration. Chronic diarrhoea is routinely worked up for EPI.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Early retatrutide 12 mg postmarketing shows the expected rise with ~29% loss.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. It is pleaded in the mass tort alongside EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after 2+ years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Lean loss is proportionally larger at ~29% total loss on retatrutide 12 mg. Bimagrumab offsets part of it in the small group that can get it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code; resistance-training statement extended to retatrutide 12 mg; bimagrumab approved as adjunct.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal. The Steadra AUD trials showed no excess.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10% on standard retatrutide and ~12% in early 12 mg data. The Steadra AUD trials used a narrow anhedonia scale and found no excess at low dose, and platforms cite this. The FDA postmarketing observational study slipped to 2035.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Still unlabelled. OPDP sent Novo an untitled letter (Nov 2033) over Steadra ads that implied general calm, and a warning letter to one telehealth platform. No enforcement action followed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Elastase-holiday takers regain on the same curve, and waiver drop-outs regain fastest.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and conditional coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency; fat-soluble deficiency with EPI. Deficiency is more frequent at retatrutide 12 mg intake levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel labelling retained and added to retatrutide.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Partial elastase recovery in about half of people after 12+ months off is what drives the 'holiday' practice. Tirzepatide at 6+ years now shows a smaller but significant excess (HR ~1.4). Unsealed documents show Novo's internal 2026–27 extension-cohort faecal-elastase analyses reached the FDA about two years late.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling retained. Tirzepatide label updated Jun 2034. FDA warning letter to Novo (Sep 2033) for late postmarketing reporting under 21 CFR 314.80; DOJ civil investigative demand open.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent gastroparesis, ileus and pancreatic injury: mass-tort litigation
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~74,000 filed claims across the federal MDL in E.D. Pennsylvania and coordinated state proceedings, with ~120,000 more under tolling agreements, by Dec 2034. Persistent gastroparesis after stopping remains causally unproven. EPI claims rest on an established signal and, after 2033, on notice documents. First bellwether (Philadelphia, Jun 2034): $6.2M compensatory, $31M punitive, on appeal. Novo has reserved ~$4.5B; Lilly's tirzepatide exposure is smaller.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA has taken no new GI action beyond existing labels. Judicial Daubert rulings let EPI general-causation experts in and limited post-discontinuation gastroparesis claims.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling and planned holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The bone and pancreas effects of holiday-and-restart cycles are uncharacterised, and holidays are now routine advice without trial evidence.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue. No regulator has endorsed holidays.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~31,000 by late 2034. There was no outbreak on the 2031 scale. Retatrutide-analogue research vials produced a 2034 cluster of ~90 ED visits for tachycardia and dysaesthesia. Poison-centre calls are flat at ~5× 2025.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert extended to two retatrutide-analogue suppliers. CBP seizures ~3× 2030. No statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month liraglutide PMR update (2034) shows a height-velocity deficit narrowing to ~0.5 cm/yr, with partial catch-up in children who stopped. Final adult height is unknown. The ARFID signal is unchanged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Growth and Tanner monitoring labelling retained. EMA added similar wording in 2033. No age restriction.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysaesthesia and heart-rate increase at high-dose triple agonism
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Skin dysaesthesia in ~15–20% of people on retatrutide 12 mg, mostly transient. Resting heart rate rises ~5–7 bpm.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled on the Jan 2034 approval; cardiac rhythm PMR required.

food_and_beverage.state: About 37% of households have a user, roughly flat because waiver enrolment offset gray-market quitters. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~10–12% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~10%. Waiver states produced the first measurable dips in dollar-store snack volumes, in rural Tennessee and Louisiana. 'Holiday packs' (structured protein-forward meal plans for people taking a break) launched at Kroger and Hy-Vee. Zip-code assortment planning is standard.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~15% from 2025 and beer ~10%. Steadra's on-label AUD claim and its DTC campaign turned telehealth alcohol reduction from a niche into a television category. Constellation and Molson Coors wrote down mid-tier brands. NA and functional drinks grow but remain small. Bar closures spread from the Midwest into Sun Belt suburbs.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Portion-tiered menus are universal in casual dining, and bar-heavy concepts lost ~8% of beverage revenue. QSR value menus hold in non-waiver Southern markets. In waiver counties early data show small QSR traffic dips.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Retatrutide 12 mg created a market for loose-skin compression garments and alteration services. Resale and rental serve cyclers and holiday-takers, who now plan for a size swing.

fitness.state: Strength training grows. Premium DXA-plus-coaching plans add bimagrumab infusion coordination at $400–600 a month. Budget chains sell 'holiday programmes' to keep weight off during elastase breaks. Waiver states fund no fitness component.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is 27%, and most remaining coverage is conditional on verified adherence and milestones. Pharmacy trend ~+5%. Some plans now require documented holiday consultation after 5 years on semaglutide, citing litigation exposure. Part D premiums rose modestly in 2034. Product-liability insurers repriced pharma cover.

pharma.state: Lilly gained share on retatrutide 12 mg and its relative litigation insulation. Novo is hit three ways: the reporting scandal, the ~$4.5B reserve and semaglutide holidays. It offset part of that with Steadra and the waiver Foundayo-competing Wegovy pill bids, which it lost to Lilly. Amgen keeps employer tracks. Global volume is dominated by Indian and Chinese makers.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug says nothing now. Being visibly off does, and people volunteer the reason before anyone asks: 'I'm on holiday', 'my pancreas break', 'waiting on my weigh-in'. Lean with muscle still means covered and coached. Very lean with loose skin and a compression sleeve marks the new 12 mg cohort. In waiver counties a soft, slowly shrinking body with a phone check-in reminder is the public-programme body.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin, 'off-drug lean' lost some cachet once holidays made going off routine. The new elite marker is a bimagrumab-preserved DXA through a 29% loss. In Memphis the visible change is that cyclers are fewer. Shelby County health department Foundayo clinics drew vial users in, and the people now marked as poor are those cut from the waiver at six months, who are back on Telegram vials. Upper-income parents still keep prepubertal children off.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Hosts ask 'on or holiday?' the way they once asked about allergies. Bread Alone claims ~700 congregations and runs 'holiday fellowships' for people in breaks. In waiver states, church suppers adapted with smaller plates and protein dishes promoted by health department outreach.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps dropped the 'on a calm plan' tag as too common and added 'on holiday until…'. People ask about an elastase holiday the way they once asked about a gap year. Partners plan around a holiday partly because desire and appetite return together.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Normalised: appetite is a setting, and a returning appetite is a scheduled event. Unmuted reframed itself around the scandal ('they knew about your pancreas'), the MAHA wing joined in, and fat-acceptance revivalists still stand apart.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Anhedonia ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–12% on retatrutide. ~2.1M people on calm/focus plans, a growing share of them written as Steadra on an AUD screening questionnaire (AUDIT-C ≥4), which makes the product partly on-label. Rates at low doses outside AUD populations remain unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Novo's Steadra campaign 'Quiet the pull' is the first manufacturer marketing to name reduced craving as the benefit. Platforms extend it to 'quiet mind'. HR says steadiness. Clinicians say dose-related side effect. Unmuted calls it a sedative that is now advertised on Sunday football.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~6.4M employees sit in adherence-verified tracks. Brokers bundle de-identified 'focus cohort' data into wellness RFPs. One of the two EEOC ADA charges got a right-to-sue letter in 2034 and a federal suit is pending in Ohio. Upper-tier staff list 'Steadra protocol' alongside sleep tracking, and some sales teams now complain about colleagues being 'too even' to close.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' writing, the diary of the twelve months off, replaced 'off' memoir. Sportsbook handle per account is down again. Bars in Austin advertise 'holiday nights'. Ambient streaming genres are steady.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still the leading couples complaint. Holidays create a new pattern: a partner who suddenly wants more, more food, more sex, more argument, for a year, then goes back on.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The live fights are the Novo documents, which drew Senate HELP hearings and state AG letters but no statute, and the waiver milestone rules, attacked by Tennessee and Louisiana Democrats as 'lose weight or lose the pill'. The 2034 midterms featured candidates' own drug status as unremarkable trivia. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive with more paper. FDA approved Steadra, retatrutide 12 mg and bimagrumab, sent Novo a reporting warning letter and sent OPDP untitled letters over calm-adjacent advertising. DOJ has a civil investigation open. No state acted on adherence premiums beyond Illinois, and Congress held hearings only.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: New subsidy, with conditions attached. CMS approved 'Metabolic Health' 1115 waivers in five states (Oct 2033), giving free Foundayo to ~0.8M low-income adults at ~$1.33B/yr (~$0.9B federal), conditional on weekly app check-ins and ≥5% loss at six months. The 2027 30% premium guidance stands. No federal mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is now public as well as private. Waiver apps log check-ins, weigh-ins at health departments and pharmacy pickups, and the state Medicaid data warehouses hold the records. Employer tracks keep clinic-administration feeds. Calm platforms sell de-identified mood data, now tagged with AUDIT-C scores.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged and the Army oral pilot continues. In 2034 DOT issued interpretive guidance that on-label Steadra is not disqualifying for commercial drivers when it is disclosed to the medical examiner, and said nothing about off-label calm use.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply ~70% of world volume. US–India talks remain stalled. Chinese retatrutide analogues were added to the import alert and Beijing protested again. The cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–50×.

events.event: FDA approves Novo's low-dose oral semaglutide as Steadra for alcohol use disorder, the first label to claim reduced craving; within months telehealth calm platforms write it on screening questionnaires and 'Quiet the pull' ads run nationally

Documents unsealed in the incretin MDL show Novo's internal 2026–27 faecal-elastase analyses reached the FDA about two years late; an FDA warning letter follows in September and DOJ opens a civil investigation
CMS approves 'Metabolic Health' Medicaid waivers in Tennessee, Louisiana, West Virginia, Oklahoma and Arkansas: free Foundayo for low-income adults who check in weekly and lose 5% by six months
Business Group on Health finds employer weight-loss coverage down to 27%, with seven in ten remaining plans requiring verified adherence and BMI milestones; monitored tracks reach 6.4 million workers
FDA approves a 12 mg maintenance dose of Lilly's retatrutide, 14 months after its Nov 2032 filing, labelling ~29% mean weight loss; Lilly sets cash price at $299 in April's TrumpRx repricing
A Philadelphia jury awards $37.2M, $31M of it punitive, in the first pancreatic-insufficiency bellwether against Novo; filed claims pass 70,000 and Novo reserves ~$4.5B

open_tensions: Planned 'elastase holidays' are now routine advice for long-term semaglutide users, with no trial behind them. About 1.4M people are off on schedule and regaining on the usual curve, and nobody knows what holiday-and-restart cycles do to bone or pancreas.
The waiver states' 5% six-month milestone means the people the subsidy fails are cut off. About half of them return to the vial channel that the subsidy was built to drain.

Steadra made craving reduction an on-label claim, and ~2.1M people buy a calm that is partly prescribed on a drinking questionnaire. Employers are buying the mood data, and the low-dose anhedonia study has slipped to 2035.

Retatrutide 12 mg delivers surgical-scale loss at $299 a month in cash. The muscle-sparing adjunct costs ~$1,150 and reaches mainly the covered upper tier, while fracture risk concentrates in 60-year-olds paying cash.

prose.headline: Nobody Asks Why You're On It Anymore. They Ask Why You Stopped.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about nineteen in every hundred American adults take an incretin, roughly fifty-two million people. That is slightly fewer than two years ago, though the drugs have never been more ordinary. Three in ten adults have tried one. Nobody remarks on being on it. Being off is what people explain, and they usually explain it before anyone asks.

The usual explanation is a holiday. In August 2033, documents unsealed in the pancreatic litigation showed that Novo Nordisk's own analyses of long-term users had flagged falling pancreatic enzyme levels years before the company sent them to regulators. The warning letter, the federal investigation and a thirty-seven-million-dollar Philadelphia verdict followed. More than seventy thousand people have now filed claims. Doctors who had read that about half of patients recover partial enzyme function after a year off began advising long-term semaglutide users to take that year. About a million and a half are now on their break, and most of them are regaining on schedule.

Who pays is still decided by conditions. Only 27 percent of employers cover the drugs for weight loss, and most of those pay only while a record shows the patient took the dose and lost the weight. Six and a half million workers are in monitored tracks, many getting a monthly shot from a nurse at the plant clinic. The newest conditions are public. In October 2033 Medicare's administrators approved waivers in Tennessee, Louisiana, West Virginia, Oklahoma and Arkansas that give a daily pill free to low-income adults. In exchange they check in on an app each week and lose five percent by the six-month weigh-in. Eight hundred thousand people enrolled, many of them people who had been injecting vials bought on Telegram. Those who miss the target lose the pill, and about half of them go back to the vials.

Prices kept stepping down where manufacturers and the government's cash channel agreed they would. Maintenance pills cost under two hundred dollars a month and injectables under three hundred. The list price on the box has not changed. In January 2034 Lilly won approval for a higher dose of its triple agonist that takes off almost thirty percent of body weight, surgical results from a pen, at $299 a month in cash. A new antibody that protects some muscle during the loss costs four times that, and it reaches mostly people with covered coaching plans.

The calm market became official. In March 2033 the FDA approved a low-dose semaglutide pill, sold as Steadra, for people who drink more than they mean to. It was the first label to promise less craving, and the advertising, 'Quiet the pull', runs on Sunday football. Telehealth platforms now write it after a four-question drinking survey. Two million people pay for some form of quiet, and the study that would say what it costs them in pleasure has been pushed back to 2035.

The country sorts as it did before, with new sorting rules. In Charlotte and Austin the boast is having lost thirty percent while keeping your muscle on the scan. Along the Columbus freight corridor the shot comes monthly at the clinic and the record goes to the vendor. In Memphis the county health department hands out free pills, and the people still buying vials are those the programme dropped. Spirits sales are down by about a sixth since 2025. Bars advertise holiday nights. Parents in the upper tier still keep young children off the drugs, and the growth gap in those who started young has narrowed but not closed.

Congress held hearings and passed nothing. No state followed Illinois. It looks like a functioning system, and it is one, built on conditions.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
LaToya Briggs wakes at 5:40 in Frayser and takes the Foundayo from the blister card on the sink. The TennCare app pings before her coffee: Check-in due. Mood 1–5. Hunger 1–5. She gives both a three, as she always does.

Her first client is Mr. Pruitt on Watkins, who is ninety and asks about her weight every morning. He calls it her government diet. She bathes him and makes his oatmeal, then eats half a boiled egg in the car.

At one she sits on a plastic chair at the Shelby County health department and waits for the six-month weigh-in. The woman ahead of her comes out crying quietly into her phone. LaToya started at 241 pounds and needs to be at 229 or under. The scale shows 230.4. The nurse, whose lanyard reads Metabolic Health Program, types something, looks at the screen for a while and types again.

"We can do a fourteen-day recheck," she says. "Some people come in fasting."

LaToya's cousin Dre texts during her afternoon client: if they cut u i still got the guy. He means the vials from the Telegram shop, the kind that put his neighbour in Methodist for a week in 2031.

At home her daughter Kiara, nineteen, is eating cereal and watching a Steadra ad on her phone, a woman on a porch while the music softens. Kiara says half her shift at the Amazon facility is on something.

"You're not," LaToya says.

"I'm on holiday," Kiara says, and laughs, because she has never been on anything.

At nine LaToya skips dinner and sets an alarm for the recheck.
